Hello Stephanie, how are we today?
Doing okay, I suppose.
Okay, so I see that you made the appointment today because of an ongoing problem.
Why don't you tell me more about it?
Yes, um, I have been feeling a lot of fatigue over the last six months or so.
At first I brushed it off. I mean, after all, I am an infant school teacher
and most of my colleagues complain of feeling tired at the end of many days.
So what got you to the point of coming in for an appointment?
Hmm. I have been spending a lot of my spare time taking classes at my local gym,
but recently I've been coming up with reasons not to go to them.
After skipping them three days in a row, I decided that I needed to do something.
And do you smoke or drink regularly?
I never smoke. How disgusting.
So a non-smoker. Got it.
I sometimes have a drink, like at a party, but only once a week or so.
Also, I don't know if this is important, but I have been mostly vegetarian for the last five years.
I do often eat fish and also dairy.
So let's start to get to the bottom of this.
Other than the tiredness, have you been experiencing any other symptoms?
Nothing that I can think of. What type of symptom?
Like abdominal pain or a change in appetite?
No, nothing like that.
I do sometimes have some issues in the bathroom. Like I have a bowel movement like three times a
day and I don't know if that is normal. Also sometimes it can be difficult to flush everything
down. Is that normal? Frequent and large bowel movements. That does point to something that
could be important. It appears that you're experiencing malabsorption. So what I need to do
is order some investigations to find a cause. Let's go back a bit to family history. Do you
have any history of abdominal problems in your family? Yes, I think so. My grandmother, the one
who lived in Ireland, died three years ago and I think she had some bowel problems. But to be honest,
I don't know the specifics of her death. So with the investigations, what would you actually be
looking for? Well, the first thing would be to see if your white cell count, haemoglobin, platelets
and the like are within normal ranges. Anemia, which would be indicated by a low level of
hemoglobin is a common cause of tiredness, but of course we would then still need to figure out the
cause of it. And what are some of the common causes of malabsorption? What might we be looking at here?
Well, one possibility worth considering is celiac disease, particularly since you mentioned that your
Irish grandmother had some bowel problems. Celiac disease is four times more common in Ireland than
in the rest of the UK, and there is a genetic component to this disease. And would the results
of the investigations be enough to diagnose me with celiac disease? No, I'm afraid they would
not be enough. Depending on the results of the investigations, we would then have to do an
endoscopy and biopsy to confirm a diagnosis of celiac disease. Unfortunately, there's no simple
blood test we can do. Are there any other possible diagnoses? Yes, but I would prefer to wait to talk
about other possibilities until we have the results of the investigations. So we can go ahead
and take your blood today and that way we would get the results back by Monday.
Are you available for a follow-up appointment on Monday?
I think so, but just let me check my calendar.
So, let's see.

So I have here the chest x-ray that was taken when you were admitted.
So here I can see a dilated, fluid-filled esophagus with no visible gastric air bubble.
This explains your respiratory issues.
How so? How is my esophagus related to my lungs?
Well, food is spilling over from your esophagus into your lung, which has caused your episodes of respiratory infections.
You said earlier you had them in the right side, and this is consistent with spillover from the esophagus.
But I had that endoscopy done and it didn't show anything at all.
Yes, it seems you had the endoscopy done at the early stage, so that is why it didn't pick anything up.
So what is the diagnosis? Do you have a name for this?
Well, I want to do a few more tests, but the likely diagnosis is accalasia of the cardia,
which is a neurological disturbance of the intersecting nerves at the lower end of your esophagus.
Other common causes are benign esophageal structures from acid reflux,
malignant structures or an esophageal pouch.
OK, and what would the treatment for this problem?

what we do know is that human milk contains multiple biologically active components,

contribute to stress during adolescence include a desire for greater autonomy, as well as pressure

What about teens who are diagnosed early with a mental health condition? How does this affect them?

While early detection and treatment is always good, adolescents with mental health conditions are particularly vulnerable to social exclusion, discrimination, stigma, in addition to educational difficulties, risk-taking behaviours and poor physical health.
So what can be done to support teens during this confusing period in their lives?
This period of life is crucial for developing and maintaining social and emotional habits, important for wellbeing.

The first course of action is mental health promotion and prevention interventions that aim to strengthen individuals' capacity to regulate emotions,
enhance alternatives to risk-taking behaviours, and build resilience into difficult situations.
